question: Which antimicrobial enzymes are present in milk?
solution:
The correct answer is** __Lectoferrin, lactoperoxidase, and lysozyme.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​​​In human milk, **a number of antibacterial enzymes** have been found. An antimicrobial "oxidative enzyme system" made up of xanthine oxidase (XO) and lactoperoxidase (LPO) is crucial for developing early immunity.
 
• Another important** antibacterial enzyme is lysozyme.**
 
• **Lysozyme, lactoferrin, lactoperoxidase, **and **immunoglobulins **are the main antimicrobial proteins found in milk. In the section on Inhibitors in Milk, these have been **briefly discussed.** A folate binding protein and several small proteins have been identified in **some species.**
 
• In conjunction with** lactoferrin, lactoperoxidase fights halitosis**; in conjunction with** lysozyme and lactoferrin, lactoperoxidase** aids in alleviating** xerostomia symptoms.** Additionally, lactoperoxidase gels can aid with oral cancer symptoms when irradiation has affected **saliva production.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​​​​​​​​Among the** primary digestive enzymes produced by the pancreas **are Amylase (made in the mouth and pancreas; breaks down complex carbohydrates)** Lipase** (made in the pancreas; breaks down fats) **Protease** (made in the pancreas; breaks down proteins).
 
• Two different kinds of **sugar, lactose and fructose**, are found naturally in milk and fruit, respectively. They make up a sizable portion of your daily sugar intake, and the** human body can typically absorb them**. Microbes, plants, and mammals all contain** mannose.**
 
• The **body employs the enzyme **lipase to digest dietary fats so they may be absorbed in the intestines. The pancreas, mouth, and stomach** all manufacture lipase. ****​**​​​​​​​
